description: A seven-stage binary ripple counter: each output halves the rate of the one before it, from the clock divided by two down to the clock divided by 128.

inputs.text: A falling edge advances the count by one; the count wraps round to 0 once every output has been high together.
While this is high the count is held at 0 and every output is at 0V.

outputs.text: Changes state on every falling clock edge, so it carries the clock divided by two.
Changes state on every second falling clock edge, so it carries the clock divided by four.
Changes state on every fourth falling clock edge, so it carries the clock divided by eight.
Changes state on every eighth falling clock edge, so it carries the clock divided by sixteen.
Changes state on every sixteenth falling clock edge, so it carries the clock divided by thirty-two.
Changes state on every thirty-second falling clock edge, so it carries the clock divided by sixty-four.
Changes state on every sixty-fourth falling clock edge, so it carries the clock divided by 128.

notes: A logic input counts as high once it rises above 2V and does not count as low again until it falls below 0.1V; a logic output is 10V for high and 0V for low.
The counter advances on the falling edge of the clock, so an output changes as the clock goes low rather than as it goes high.

inputs.0:
high above 2V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
